extracted.intended_audience: Researchers, journal editors, funders and other stakeholders involved in planning, conducting, reviewing or publishing in vivo (animal) research
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting (and for planning/conducting) in vivo animal studies to improve transparency, reproducibility and assessment of risk of bias. Emphasises a prioritized 'Essential 10' minimum reporting set plus a complementary 'Recommended Set'.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARRIVE Essential 10
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'ARRIVE Essential 10' that are the basic minimum to include in a manuscript to enable readers and reviewers to assess the reliability of the findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The major shift is the prioritisation of the recommendations into two groups to simplify their use in practice — focus initial efforts on the Essential 10. The Essential 10 highlight items related to potential risk of bias and serve an important step toward better study design, experimental rigor, and improved reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Set
rubrics_metrics.description: The complementary 'Recommended Set' that provides context to the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to be adopted subsequently as best reporting practice after initial focus on the Essential 10; provides contextual information to accompany the Essential 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report experimental design and statistical analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Include information on experimental design and statistical analyses, for example, sample size calculations and strategies to minimise bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A major barrier to transparent reporting is a lack of understanding about the importance of including these details; omitting them has consequences for reproducibility and reliability. The Explanation and Elaboration document describes the relevance of each item with examples of good practice taken from the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full, transparent reporting to enable scrutiny and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting must be full and transparent so that research can be properly scrutinised or reproduced; poor reporting negatively influences reliability and reproducibility and wastes animal use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical and scientific imperative: without sufficient information readers and reviewers cannot assess reliability. Responsibility lies with researchers and organisations to embrace ARRIVE 2.0 and associated resources to ensure poor reporting of in vivo research is a thing of the past.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use guidelines for planning, conduct and recording of studies
rubrics_metrics.description: ARRIVE guidelines can be used during the planning and conduct of animal studies to help make sure that experiments are robustly designed and properly recorded, preparing the way for future publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although primarily to improve manuscripts, the guidelines are also a tool for improving experimental design and record-keeping during study planning and conduct; developed by an international working group and prioritised via a Delphi exercise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation and Elaboration resource
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'explanation and elaboration' document accompanies the guidelines and describes the relevance of each item with examples of good practice taken from the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this companion document for detailed rationale, examples and clarification of each guideline item; it is intended to aid understanding of why methodological details are critical in a manuscript.
